name: Messenger to Stormwind
summary: In Stormwind, you carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital sends no troops while its leaders delay, leaving the settlement exposed.

sections.title: A Dispatch to Lakeshire
sections.body: You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his first reply back to Redridge while he waits for the throne's approval. Without royal permission, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens still have no city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling to the Blackrock clan.

sections.title: Unease in the Kingdom
sections.body: Magistrate Solomon finds no promise of battalions marching east along the Elwynn border in Jonathan's reply. The letter offers procedure instead of troops, and Solomon senses trouble in the royal court. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and the regency is deadlocked. Outlying towns such as Lakeshire must defend themselves.

faq.q: What is in General Marcus Jonathan's response?
faq.answer: General Marcus Jonathan's letter says he cannot send the Stormwind army without formal authorization from the King or royal court. He has raised the matter with the crown, leaving Lakeshire to wait.

faq.q: Why can't Stormwind just send soldiers to Redridge?
faq.answer: With King Varian Wrynn missing, governing decisions rest with young King Anduin, Regent Lord Bolvar Fordragon, and the House of Nobles. Division and delay in the capital keep General Jonathan from marching without royal approval.
Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire and the Redridge Mountains. He leads the settlement and coordinates its scant defenses against Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands.
General Marcus Jonathan commands the Stormwind City Guard and the capital's standing armed forces. He is stationed at the Valley of Heroes, just inside Stormwind City's main gates.

faq.q: What does Solomon do next after reading the letter?
faq.answer: After reading the letter, Solomon seeks help from neighboring regions and sends you to learn how Westfall fares.

faq.q: Why does Solomon say 'something is amiss in our Kingdom'?
faq.answer: Solomon sees no military sense in refusing or delaying aid to a border town under attack. The delay warns him that Stormwind's political leaders are being manipulated or paralyzed from within.

angles.text: As a human of the kingdom, you carry this correspondence between guarded Stormwind City and the crumbling borders of its Elwynn neighbors.
As an Alliance member, you see how political deadlock leaves the kingdom's human territories exposed to regional threats.
